The pedestrian’s statement is admissible under the excited utterance exception because it was made immediately after the accident while the pedestrian was still under the stress of observing it, and the pedestrian’s unavailability or lack of identification does not bar admission. It is not admissible as a statement of then-existing mental, emotional, or physical condition if offered to prove the man’s negligence, since it is an opinion about fault rather than a factual observation.  
CONFIDENCE: 70
